*Source: [Polished Leadership](https://www.drivethrurpg.com/en/product/585162/diamond-polished-spheres-leadership-sphere)*

*Practitioners of the Leadership sphere learn to identify and leverage talent – from a humble smith that makes the sharpest blades to loyal brothers in arms.*

**Associated Skill (choose one):** Diplomacy or Profession (any).

**Associated Feat:** Leadership.

When you first gain the Leadership sphere, choose either the cohort or follower package. You gain the chosen package’s benefits.

The Leadership sphere uses its associated skill in place of the practitioner’s base attack bonus to determine its effects.

**[Utility Start]** When you first gain this sphere, if you select the follower package, you may gain the base Leadership sphere as a utility talent.

---

## Cohort Package

You gain the *recruit* sphere ability.

Full details and information about *recruiting* a cohort and cohort statistics are detailed in the Leadership Appendix, **About Cohorts**.

### Recruit

*You recruit a loyal and capable cohort to your aid.*

**Action:** 8 hours
**Duration:** instantaneous

**Effect:** While in a settlement, you can gain the services of a cohort. You can only have the service of 1 cohort at a given time, and must release that cohort before attempting to *recruit* a new one.

A cohort may be released from your service at any time. A cohort that leaves your service on good terms may become a contact.

You may modify this ability with a (recruit) option. Only 1 (recruit) option can be added to each use of *recruit*.

## Follower Package [utility]

You gain the ability to attract followers and the *make camp* sphere ability. In addition, you gain 1 (follower) talent that grants a follower as a bonus talent.

Full details and information about your camp and followers are detailed in the Leadership Appendix, **About Camp and Followers**.

### Make Camp

*The fire is lit and the camp bustles with energy.*

**Action:** 1 hour
**Duration:** instantaneous

**Effect:** You set up camp and your followers perform common camp tasks, including but not limited to caring for the pack animals, cooking, maintenance, and setting up temporary structures (tents and the like). When you *make camp* in a settlement, this is instead represented as gathering your followers at a tavern or other establishment to discuss travel plans and perform upkeep and maintenance.

When you *make camp*, you can gain your follower’s assistance, as detailed in each (follower) talent.

---

## Leadership Sphere-Specific Tags

The Polished Leadership sphere introduces a number of tags unique to this sphere.

- A **(cohort)** option grants a leader new ways to interact with their *recruited* cohorts or grants additional abilities, benefits, and options to both the leader and their cohorts.
- A **(follower)** option either grants a new follower or improves your ability to *make camp*.
- A **(recruit)** option modifies the *recruit* sphere ability, either improving your ability to *recruit* or allowing you to provide other benefits when you *recruit*.

**Talents with Sphere-Specific Tags:** Polished Leadership sphere talents may have the (cohort), (follower), or (recruit) tags listed in the talent name, indicating the talent grants an option with the relevant tag.

---

## Leadership Talents

### Canny Leader [utility]

*You find the responsibilities of leadership to be second nature.*

**Prerequisite:** Hold a kingdom leadership role.

**Effect:** You may use your practitioner modifier in place of a kingdom leadership role’s usual ability score (such as Wisdom or Charisma as the High Priest). If you do not replace the leadership role’s usual ability score this way, you instead increase the benefit you provide in that leadership role by +1, +1 per 5.

In addition, you gain the following benefits based on the packages you possess:

- **(cohort):** If you assign your cohort to a leadership role in the same kingdom you hold a leadership role, your cohort also benefits from this talent (replacing the ability score or gaining a flat bonus to the benefit provided by their role).
- **(follower):** Your followers ease the transition when there is a vacancy in a leadership role. If there is a vacancy, its penalties are delayed for 1 kingdom turn, +1 kingdom turn per 10 associated skill ranks.

**Associated Feat:** Natural Ruler (*Quests and Campaigns*).

See *Ultimate Campaign*, Leadership Roles for more information.

**Example:** You could either replace the High Priest’s use of Wisdom or Charisma with your practitioner modifier (for example, Intelligence), or directly increase the bonus to Stability you provide by +1, +1 per 5 associated skill ranks.

### Expanded Leadership

You gain the Leadership sphere package you do not already possess.

**Special:** If you select the follower package this way, this talent can be taken as a [utility] talent.

### Fortunate Events [utility]

*The mandate of heaven smiles upon your kingdom, your businesses, and your cattle. It seems nothing can go wrong.*

**Prerequisites:** Own at least one building or hold a kingdom leadership role.

**Effect:** You gain the following benefits based on whether you own a building or hold a kingdom leadership role.

*Buildings*: During a downtime Event phase, if an event occurs for a building you own, you may roll twice on the applicable table and choose either result. You may only benefit from this option once each week.

*Kingdom*: During a kingdom’s Event phase, once an event’s type and danger level have been determined, you may choose to roll twice on the applicable kingdom or settlement table and choose either result. If multiple characters with a leadership role could roll twice during an Event phase, you roll that many additional dice (such as six characters having this option would roll seven times, selecting one roll).

**Associated Feat:** Fortunate Manager, Fortunate Ruler (*Quests and Campaigns*).

See *Ultimate Campaign*, Downtime and Kingdom Building for more information.

**Special - Merchant (follower):** If you have a merchant follower, you may benefit from this option each downtime Event phase, not only once per week.

### Professional Undertakings [utility]

*You take the time to study the spoken word or a new trade. Those who follow you also pick up some of the same know-how.*

Choose either Diplomacy or any one Profession skill. You gain that skill as an associated skill for the Leadership sphere.

In addition, you gain the following benefits based on the packages you possess:

- **(cohort):** Your cohorts also gain the chosen skill as an associated skill (gaining associated skill ranks based on the number of talents you possess in this sphere).
- **(follower):** For each (follower) talent you possess, you gain a +2 circumstance bonus on associated skill checks made to earn a living or to run a business (*Pathfinder Unchained*). If a follower would be unavailable, or unable to join you when you *make camp*, you do not receive this bonus.

If you possess Diplomacy as a Leadership associated skill, you may use Diplomacy in place of Profession on checks to earn a living or to run a business.

**Special:** This talent may be selected multiple times, each time choosing a new skill to gain as an associated skill.

### Village Of Mentors [utility]

*There is always a village to provide guidance and nurture.*

**Prerequisite:** Leadership sphere ((follower) package, at least 1 (follower) talent).

**Effect:** Each follower may provide, as an assistance, tutoring for another creature to learn their trade. This tutoring requires 1 hour and is spent one-on-one with the creature. Once tutored, that creature receives a number of temporary skill ranks in that follower’s skill equal to your Leadership sphere associated skill ranks (to a maximum number of ranks equal to the creature’s Hit Dice).

These temporary skill ranks last for 1 month or until a creature is tutored again. Any number of creatures may be tutored this way, but may only receive temporary ranks for a single skill at a time.

**Note:** If a follower’s skill would apply to multiple categories of that skill, such as the Blacksmith’s follower’s skill applying to any Craft skill, you must choose a single Craft skill.

## Cohort and Recruit Talents

### Aiding Coordination (cohort)

*Shoulder to shoulder and blade over blade.*

You gain the following option and stance:

#### Collaborative Aid (cohort)

**Effect:** Cohorts and leaders may take the aid another action to improve an attack roll, AC, or skill check as a swift or immediate action. An aid another action taken this way must benefit a cohort or leader.

Whenever a cohort or leader takes the aid another action for the benefit of another cohort or leader, the bonus granted increases by +1, +1 per 10 associated skill ranks.

**Associated Feat:** Swift Aid (*Advanced Player’s Guide*).

#### Leader’s Instruction (cohort) [stance]

*Watch and do as I do, or at the very least, listen.*

**Enter:** Upon entering this stance, you may use the aid another action to assist a cohort within close range.

**Benefit:** While maintaining this stance, whenever you hit with an attack action or attack of opportunity, or succeed at a combat maneuver as a non-free action, you may aid another a cohort within close range. The aid another must benefit the cohort against the struck creature (improving their attack roll, AC, or skill check against it).

### Battlefield Coordination (cohort)

*The clamor of the battlefield distracts those which are less disciplined.*

You and your cohorts gain the *cohort attack* special attack action and the *cohort bolster* and *cohort defense* sphere abilities.

#### Cohort Attack (cohort) [SAA]

**Action:** 1 melee or ranged special attack action (plus 1 joint swift action, see text)

**Effect:** You make a single attack against a target. After resolving your attack, as a joint swift action, another cohort or leader may make a single attack against the same target.

**Augment 1 mf [Opening Strike]:** The cohort or leader’s joint swift action attack may be made before your special attack action. If the joint attack hits, you gain a +2 circumstance bonus on your attack roll, +1 per 5 associated skill ranks.

#### Cohort Bolster (cohort)

**Action:** move or immediate action
**Range:** close range (25 + 5 ft./2 associated skill ranks)
**Target:** a cohort or a leader

**Effect:** If the target is dying, they are immediately stabilized.

In addition, the target gains a number of temporary hit points equal to 1d4 + your practitioner modifier, +1d4 per associated skill rank. These temporary hit points may exceed the target’s maximum hit points (up to 1 per associated skill rank + your practitioner modifier) and last until the end of the encounter. A target can only benefit from these temporary hit points once per encounter.

#### Cohort Defense (cohort)

**Action:** immediate action
**Target:** an attacked cohort or leader within your threatened area

**Effect:** You redirect the triggering attack to yourself, becoming the target for all purposes. You must be aware of the triggering attack.

**Augment 1 mf [Selfless Defense]:** You may now use this ability in response to a single-target effect, redirecting it to yourself. If you are immune to the redirected effect, you are instead staggered for 1 round, bypassing any immunity to the staggered condition you possess.

### Hunting Coordination (cohort)

*A pack hunts together.*

You gain the following options:

#### Safe Passage (cohort)

**Effect:** Cohorts and leaders do not provoke attacks of opportunity for moving through the threatened squares of creatures threatened by another cohort or leader.

**Associated Feat:** Escape Route (*Ultimate Combat*).

#### Watch Together (cohort)

**Effect:** Whenever a cohort or leader succeeds on a Perception check, each other cohort and leader within close range are also treated as succeeding on that check.

In addition, if a cohort or leader could act in a surprise round, each other cohort or leader may also act during that surprise round.

**Associated Feat:** Lookout (*Advanced Player’s Guide*).

### Logistics Coordination (cohort, recruit)

*Your army runs on good recruits and better relationships.*

You gain the following options:

#### New and Old Friends (cohort) [utility]

**Effect:** You increase the number of contacts you can maintain by an additional 1 per associated rank (now 2 contacts per associated skill rank).

While in a settlement, you may gain new contacts by attempting a Diplomacy check to gather information, using your associated skill bonus in place of your Diplomacy bonus. The DC is determined as using the optional rule **Associated Skill Checks to *Recruit* Cohorts**. On a success, you gain 1 new contact, +1 contact per 5 you exceed the DC by. You may only benefit from this once per week per settlement.

#### Quartermaster’s Skill (cohort)

**Effect:** Your cohorts treat any weapon, armor, shield, or implement they wield as though they were magical and treat its enhancement bonus as +1 higher, +1 per 10 associated skill ranks. This applies even if the equipment is not masterwork or not already magical. This cannot cause the enhancement bonus of a cohort’s equipment to exceed a +5 enhancement bonus (such as a +4 *flaming* longsword being treated as a +5 *flaming* longsword, but an already +5 weapon would not benefit).

When you first *recruit* a cohort, in addition to the cohort’s starting kit, the cohort may acquire any amount of mundane equipment for their personal use (such as more expensive armor or high Strength-rating composite longbows, subject to GM discretion). At 5 associated skill ranks, equipment acquired this way may also be made of special materials.

This option does not allow a cohort to acquire additional consumables or equipment not directly relevant to their abilities.

### Mystic Coordination (cohort)

You gain the following options, and you and your cohorts gain the *cohort delivery* sphere ability.

#### Cohort Conduit (cohort)

**Prerequisite:** casting class feature.

**Effect:** Your cohorts gain the share spells ability, allowing you to cast spells with a target of “you” on a cohort as though casting a touch spell. You may cast spells on your cohorts even if those spells do not normally affect creatures of the cohort’s type.

**Special:** This is treated as the share spells ability (as the familiar ability).

#### Cohort Delivery (cohort)

**Prerequisites:** casting class feature or supernatural ability with a range of touch (see text).
**Action:** 1 standard action
**Range:** a cohort or leader within close range

**Effect:** When you cast a spell or use a supernatural ability with a range of touch, you may transfer that spell or supernatural effect to another cohort or leader, who may deliver the effect as the “toucher”, spending their own actions to do so. If you cast another spell or use the same supernatural ability again before the effect is delivered by the toucher, the effect is lost.

**Augment 1 mf [Striking Delivery]:** When transferring a spell or supernatural effect to the toucher, the toucher may instead deliver the effect through their next successful weapon attack.

**Special:** This option is treated as the deliver touch spells ability (as the familiar ability).

#### Safeguarded Cohorts (cohort)

**Effect:** Whenever a cohort attempts a save against an effect created by their leader, they roll twice and take the better result. On a successful save, the cohort avoids all additional effects that would otherwise occur (additional saves, half damage, inflicted conditions, and so on).

### Readiness Coordination (cohort)

*Standing together with one purpose.*

You gain the following options:

#### Cohort Teamwork (cohort)

**Effect:** Your cohorts are treated as possessing any teamwork feats you possess, even if they do not meet the prerequisites of those teamwork feats.

**Associated Feat:** Practiced Leadership (*Champions of Balance*).

#### Joint Readiness (cohort)

**Effect:** When readying an action, you and your cohorts may exclude actions taken by a cohort or a leader as a trigger (such as “the next creature that walks through that door” would never trigger due to the actions of a cohort or a leader).

In addition, whenever a cohort or leader readies an action and that readied action triggers, other cohorts or the leader may take that same action as a joint action. If the action requires an attack roll or check, each participant may use the highest roll as their own roll. A readied action cannot be shared this way if the triggering action was done by a cohort or a leader.

Each participant’s action is subject to the same trigger conditions as the original readied action, but may target other creatures, provided those targets also meet the trigger (such as readying to attack any charging creature, then targeting different chargers).

**Associated Feat:** Concentrated Fire (*Inner Sea Races*).

### Temporary Conscription (recruit)

*Instead of gaining the services of a cohort, you create a bond between yourself and one of your allies.*

**Action:** 15 minutes
**Duration:** 24 hours
**Target:** 1 ally

**Effect:** The target becomes a conscripted ally for the duration. You may have up to 1 conscripted ally at a time, +1 per 5 associated skill ranks.

A conscripted ally is treated as one of your cohorts, and you are treated as their leader. A conscripted ally may benefit from (cohort) talents, except those that permanently improve or modify a cohort, such as quartermaster’s skill, talented cohorts, and training regiment. Class features or other abilities that further customize cohorts similarly do not apply to conscripted allies (such as a knight captain’s squires or a sheriff’s deputies).

If a conscripted ally becomes hostile to you for any reason, this effect is temporarily suppressed until they are no longer hostile.

### Training Coordination (cohort, recruit)

*The key to a well maintained unit is discipline and training.*

You gain the following options:

#### Talented Cohorts (cohort)

**Effect:** One cohort of your choice gains 1 additional feat. If you retrain one or more feats granted by this option, you may instead assign those feats to a different cohort in your service.

**Special:** This talent may be selected multiple times. Each time it is selected, you gain 1 additional feat to assign to a cohort.

#### Training Regiment (recruit) [utility]

**Action:** 2 hours or longer (see text)

**Effect:** Instead of *recruiting* a new cohort, you spend 2 hours to retrain one of your cohorts, reselecting 1 feat, talent, or a number of skill ranks equal to your associated skill rank. Newly selected feats, talents, and skills must be appropriate for the cohort (subject to GM discretion). A cohort can only be retrained once per day this way.

Alternatively, you may fully retrain a cohort, reselecting the cohort’s job and any number of their feats, talents, or skills. This also changes the cohort’s ability scores, as appropriate. You must spend 24 hours to fully retain a cohort this way, or 8 hours if in a settlement with access to appropriate trainers (subject to GM discretion). This retraining period may be spread across multiple sessions but is not complete until the full time is spent.
